title: Loop write visibility — a guard must see the state just written
proves: A node's result is in the Context by the time its successor runs. The guard reads `q` and `i` written by the node immediately before it, and again on every pass through the back-edge, so the loop completes exactly 24 iterations.
notes:
REGRESSION TEST for the defect found during v0.4.5 release testing. A node's result used to be handed to an unbuffered channel and applied by a consumer goroutine AFTER the send returned; in that window the task settled, its successor was queued, and the successor read the document without the write in it. The guard then saw `q` as empty, `undefined < 0` is false in JS, so it routed `done` on the first pass and the run finished in ~3ms reporting an empty result as a SUCCESS — status `finished`, zero errors.

Measured in fractal-core, A-B-A with a restart between arms: 22/400 runs wrong unpatched, 0/400 patched, 21/400 wrong when reverted. Two failure shapes, both silent: i=0 (guard exited on the first pass) and i=25 (guard read a stale counter and took an extra pass).

repeat is 100 BECAUSE the defect was intermittent at ~5% per run: a single run cleared it 95% of the time and told you nothing. 100 runs catches a 5% regression ~99.4% of the time. Each run is ~30ms of engine time, so the whole case costs well under a minute.

Needs no model, no plugin, no network and no secret — js and rule nodes only.
